Definition: from G5137; to seize by the throat or neck, i.e. to expose the gullet of a victim for killing (generally, to lay bare):--opened.
BiblicalUsage: This word has only one occurrence, and it is the most searching verse in Hebrews. All things are naked and opened — laid bare, the throat exposed — unto the eyes of Him with whom we have to do, and the Greek word for opened is the word for seizing a victim by the throat to lay its gullet bare.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the picture is meant to be felt, not softened: before God there is no covering, no hiding place, and the word for it is the word for an exposed throat.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
